clue.text: Punish having hot drink on Sabbath in church

indicators.note: the drink and the day sit inside the church abbreviation, so the church letters wrap round them

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A puritanical rebuke for someone caught sipping something hot in church on the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot drink suggests tea, but 'hot' and 'drink' are separate pieces; the drink is an Italian sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise someone is to scold or discipline them, a close synonym of inflicting a penalty.

clue.text: Stroke requires attention by senior surgeon at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset means at the start, so only the first letter of each of those words counts

blocks.note: first letters of senior and surgeon

explanation.surface: A stroke patient needs prompt attention from a senior surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroke reads as the medical emergency, but it is the gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, affectionate stroke of the hand, so the two words share the noun sense.

clue.text: Climb in Alsace regularly before death

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the region's name is kept

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of Alsace
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A mountaineer climbs in the Alsace region and dies on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsace is a region of north-east France.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up or climb, the verb sense matching the definition.

clue.text: Money man in time to restore confidence to king after loss of direction

indicators.note: loss of a compass point means one direction letter is dropped from the restoring word

blocks.note: to reassure is to restore someone's confidence
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A financier is brought in at the right moment to calm the king's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: One S (south) comes out of REASSURE; 'after' places the king last as well as marking the loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer who manages an organisation's funds, literally a person in charge of money.

clue.text: Half-length coat adopted by little sister works OK

indicators.note: half the length means only half the word's letters survive, here its second half
something adopted is taken in, so the shortened garment goes inside the sibling word

explanation.surface: A cut-down coat handed to a younger sister fits fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-length coat seems to describe a short jacket, but it tells you to keep only half the word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfactory is acceptable and adequate, which is what calling it OK means.

clue.text: Followed vehicle around England's borders

indicators.note: turned around, so the vehicle word is read from right to left
a country's borders are its edges, so only the outside letters of the name are kept

blocks.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
first and last letters of England

explanation.surface: Someone tailed a car on a drive round the edges of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Around looks like it describes the route, but it turns the vehicle word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace a person or path is to follow its course or track it down.

clue.text: Change topping of breakfast food traditionally eaten on Sunday

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for 'food traditionally eaten on Sunday'

indicators.note: changing the topping swaps the first letter of a down answer for a different one

explanation.surface: A cook alters the topping on a breakfast dish usually served on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: TOAST loses its T for an R. The Sunday roast is a traditional British weekend lunch of roasted meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast dinner of meat and vegetables is the classic British meal served at Sunday lunchtime.

clue.text: Broad-minded churchgoer

blocks.note: first meaning: wide-ranging and inclusive in tastes
second meaning: a member of the Roman church

explanation.walkthrough: With a lower-case c the word means universal in taste; with a capital it names the Roman church's members.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are wide-ranging and liberal, while a Catholic is a worshipper in the Roman Catholic faith.

clue.text: Sacking of corrupt GP is done

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest family doctor is struck off and dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' is the verb form, matching the -ING answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposing someone means removing them from office or power, the same as dismissing or sacking them.

clue.text: Revive damaged acer tree

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener tries to nurse a damaged maple back to health.
explanation.walkthrough: An acer is a maple, which makes 'acer tree' read naturally while the two words are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate something is to bring it back into being, much as reviving restores something lost.

clue.text: Overtake most senior PC

blocks.note: in a race, to lap someone is to overtake them a full circuit ahead
the top person is the most senior

explanation.surface: A police constable jumps ahead of a senior officer in the pecking order.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable; here it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer, the kind of machine abbreviated as a PC.

clue.text: Tactless for peacekeepers to join ambassador in charge

blocks.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops joining up with an ambassador in command would be a tactless move.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undiplomatic lacks the tact and sensitivity needed in handling people, so is blunt and tactless.

clue.text: Goes down the drains

blocks.note: first meaning: descends, as a ship under water
second meaning: basins with plugholes in kitchens

explanation.surface: Something disappears down the plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, 'goes down the drain'; split it into a verb and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means descends below the surface; as a plural noun it names basins with drains in kitchens.

clue.text: Authorises son to take steps to protect name

indicators.note: something protecting another thing surrounds it, so the steps word wraps round the name letter

explanation.surface: A parent approves measures to safeguard the family name.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside ACTIONS after its first letter, and S comes in front: SANCTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to give it official permission or approval, which is what authorising does.

clue.text: Establishment newspaper is into a restructuring

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds something in a new form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group

explanation.surface: A paper is in the middle of a corporate shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like it places one thing inside another, but it is just letters for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment can be an institution or body, the same sense as an organisation such as a company or society.

clue.text: Space traveller advanced to Saturn in error

indicators.note: something done in error comes out wrong, so the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A spacefarer mistakenly heads on towards Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a person trained to travel beyond Earth's atmosphere in a spacecraft.

clue.text: Beetles start to scratch those in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: campers stay in tents or caravans

explanation.surface: Insects begin scratching at people sleeping in tents.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetles is a verb here: to beetle off is to hurry along.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to move quickly with short steps, which is just what someone who scampers does.

clue.text: Created trendy outlet with comedian at its heart

indicators.note: a word's heart is its centre, so only its two middle letters are used

blocks.note: a vent is an opening for air or gas to escape

explanation.surface: A fashionable venue was set up with a comic as its star act.
explanation.walkthrough: Outlet sounds like a shop, but here it is an escape opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent something is to create or devise it for the first time, so invented means created.

clue.text: After catching rat unexpectedly, uncle got a pat on the back

indicators.note: what happens unexpectedly comes in a surprising order, so the relative's words are rearranged
one thing catching another holds it, so the rodent goes inside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: An uncle is praised for unexpectedly catching a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: The rodent is not part of the rearrangement: only the uncle's words are mixed, and the rat sits whole in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat on the back is praise for an achievement, and to congratulate is to offer exactly that praise.

clue.text: Stay in hostel in Germany

indicators.note: in here means contained within the words that follow, spanning them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A traveller stops over at a German youth hostel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' reads as part of the sentence; the second is part of the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on longer than expected, reluctant to leave.

clue.text: Man extremely likeable and kind-hearted

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its outermost letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of likeable

explanation.surface: A man described as very likeable and good-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremely reads as an intensifier for likeable, but it selects that word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle person is mild and tender in manner, close to being kind-hearted.

clue.text: Doctor alerts mom to very confused state of affairs

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor warns a mother that things are in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician; it is the instruction to tamper with the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is literally a whirlpool and figuratively a turbulent, chaotic situation.

clue.text: European Commission is upset about Norway after that time

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down answer reads the words bottom to top
about means around, so the reversed letters surround the country

blocks.note: N is the international code for Norway

explanation.surface: Brussels has been upset about Norway ever since a certain moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset reads as annoyed, but in a down clue it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Since means from a past moment until now, the same as after that time.

clue.text: Love to be a girl

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A wistful wish to be a girl, or to be loved like one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' joins O to the verb; 'be' itself supplies LIVE. Olive is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Scope for former partner to get somewhere to sleep

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a tent is a shelter for sleeping in when camping

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is looking for a place to stay the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent and scope both mean the range or reach over which something applies.

clue.text: Frank is right about answer after serious thought, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words just before it
about means surrounding, so the direction word goes round the answer letter
after places the surrounded word behind the opening letters

blocks.note: first letters of serious and thought

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank reaches the correct answer after careful thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being straight with someone means being honest and direct, which is what frank means.

clue.text: Waterlogged piece of earth next to cave

blocks.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is an animal's cave or lair

explanation.surface: A patch of soggy ground beside a cave mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden ground is soaked through, saturated with water just as waterlogged soil is.

clue.text: Strange secret of not having to pay anything

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are put into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shares the odd secret of never paying for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT was an old tax, so going scot-free first meant escaping payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free means escaping without penalty or charge, originally without paying a tax.
